candidates.api_shape: pin_tumbler(n, pin_d, shear_heights, key_bitting) -> {cylinder, plug, key_pins, drivers, springs, key}
candidates.fdm: Oversized teaching cylinder. Prints. Springs bought or printed coil. Cutaway optional. Thingiverse default lock demo.
candidates.name: pin_tumbler
candidates.why: Yale pin tumbler. The coded shear-line cell. Not a detent (no code) and not a shaft_key (no tumblers). The missing lock primitive.

candidates.api_shape: lever_tumbler(n, gate_offsets, stump) -> {levers, bolt, stump, key}
candidates.fdm: Flat levers with a gate slot, a bolt stump. Prints flat. Chubb / mortise cell.
candidates.name: lever_tumbler
candidates.why: Lever lock. Gates must align for the stump to pass. Distinct from pin tumbler (no plug, no shear line). British furniture and safe-deposit default.

candidates.api_shape: combination_pack(n_discs, gate_w, fence) -> {discs, fence, bolt} plus a dial law
candidates.fdm: Stacked discs with one gate each, a fence. Prints. Padlock / safe cell. Dial sequence is the pose.
candidates.name: combination_pack
candidates.why: Coded discs, no key. The combination primitive. detent_pair is a single click, not a pack of gates.

candidates.api_shape: rotating discs with a sidebar that drops into aligned gates (Abloy)
candidates.fdm: Discs + sidebar. Prints. High-security teaching cell.
candidates.name: disc_detainer
candidates.why: Disc detainer. Sidebar, not a shear line and not a fence on a bolt. The other rotating-disc lock.

candidates.api_shape: a keyway with obstacle wards; the key is the negative
candidates.fdm: Prints. Oldest lock. Weak, but the named historical cell.
candidates.name: warded_keyway
candidates.why: Wards. The key must miss obstacles. No tumblers. Teaching / antique.

candidates.api_shape: flat wafers instead of round pin stacks, same shear line
candidates.fdm: Prints. Car-door / cabinet. A pin_tumbler(style='wafer') argument.
candidates.name: wafer_tumbler
candidates.why: Wafer lock. Same shear-line idea, flat tumblers. Do not add a second module if pin_tumbler can emit wafers.

candidates.api_shape: a U-shackle plus locking balls or a claw
candidates.fdm: Prints. The body is whichever tumbler cell. Getting product-shaped.
candidates.name: padlock_shackle
candidates.why: Shackle + balls. The padlock is a product around a tumbler. A thin shackle kit after the cell exists.

candidates.name: lockset_product
candidates.why: A door lockset. The reusable part is pin_tumbler.

candidates.name: detent_as_lock
candidates.why: A positional click, not a coded constraint.

rejected.name: electronic_lock
rejected.why: Solenoid + firmware. Hardware / out of scope.

rejected.name: magnetic_lock
rejected.why: Bought magnets. Same reject as magnetic_clutch.

rejected.name: safe_product
rejected.why: A box around a combination_pack. Product.

summary:
A lock is a constraint that a coded input (key, discs, or word) lifts. The usual taxonomy is by the obstacle: wards (the key must miss them), lever tumblers (gates must line up on a stump), pin tumblers (Yale: pin stack splits at a shear line), wafers (flat pins), disc detainers (Abloy: rotating discs, a sidebar drops into gates), and combination packs (discs with gates, no key). Padlock shackles add locking balls or a claw. 507 barely names locks. Reuleaux does not. Howell's 'lock' is a snap or a bistable, already in-tree as snap_catch / bistable_beam.

Catalog has no tumbler, ward, or combination pack. Neighbours: detent_pair (a click, not a coded shear), shaft_key (DIN machine key, not a lock key), pawl_latch (proposed, slam catch), geneva_stop (winding limit), dog_clutch (positive drive). Grep of usecases.py hits 'lock' only as self-locking screws, folding-leg clicks, and over-center clamps.

FDM reality. pin_tumbler is a cylinder, a plug, n pin stacks (key pin + driver + spring), and a shear line; prints oversized for teaching (Thingiverse cutaways). lever_tumbler is a stack of flat levers with gates and a bolt stump; Chubb cell, prints flat. combination_pack is n discs with a gate and a fence; the padlock/safe cell. disc_detainer is rotating discs plus a sidebar. warded is a keyway with obstacles, the oldest and the weakest. wafer is a flat pin tumbler. A lockset, a mortise body, or a safe is a product. Magnetic and electronic locks are hardware.
title: Locks, keys, and combination mechanisms
